parts.text:
Set up module `github.com/example/mapq` (Go wasn't installed, so I installed Go 1.27.1 to `~/go-sdk`; use `export PATH="$HOME/go-sdk/bin:$PATH"`).

Files:
- `path.go` — path parser: dotted/bracket paths, slice indices, quoted keys (`users[1]["first.name"]`).
- `map.go` — fluent core: `New`/`Wrap`, `Get`, `Set` (auto-creates nested maps/slices), `Delete`, `Has`, `Update`, `Apply`, `Merge`, `Clone`, `Keys`, `ForEach`, `Sub`/`Map`; errors latch and are read via `Err()`/`Done()`.
- `accessors.go` — `String`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Int64`, `Float64`, `Slice`, `StringSlice`, `IsNil`, `FromJSON`/`JSON`.
- `mapq_test.go` — 13 tests covering paths, traversal, mutation, coercion, errors, JSON.

Usage:
```go
m := mapq.New().Set("user.name", "Ada").Set("tags[1]", "go")
m.String("user.name")        // "Ada"
m.Int("tags[1]", -1)         // -1 (tags[1] is "go")
m.Sub("user").Set("age", 36)
```

`go vet`, `gofmt`, and `go test -cover` all pass (69.6% coverage). Two notes: the module path is a placeholder (`github.com/example/mapq`) — change it with `go mod edit -module ...`; and I did not add a README per convention (Go doc comments cover usage).
